clue.text: The Parisian on Northern Ireland river

indicators.note: in this convention one thing on another comes after it, so the French article is placed second

parts.note: NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland
le is French for 'the', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A French visitor is talking about some river in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style charade 'on' means placed after, so the French article follows the abbreviation even though the clue mentions it first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great African river flowing north through Egypt.

clue.text: In bar, señor prepared questions that are very easy to answer

definitions.text: questions that are very easy to answer

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written, ignoring the tilde

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman in a bar has got some easy quiz questions ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is an informal term for a problem or choice so simple it needs no thought.

clue.text: Ring up about first of images in colour

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards
about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of images

explanation.surface: Someone phones about the first set of pictures to come out in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: What may show twenty with chap bagging a run?

indicators.note: bagging means capturing and holding inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a score is twenty
bod is British slang for a person or chap
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A cricket-flavoured riddle about what displays a total of twenty when a batsman adds a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a scoreboard is what may show the score, and 'twenty' does double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard is the large display at a sports ground that shows the current score of a game.

clue.text: Ring about name on top of yellow funnel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ringing word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to ring a bell is to chime
N is the standard abbreviation for name

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of yellow

explanation.surface: Instructions for painting a bell or a ship's funnel with a yellow top.
explanation.definitionFit: A funnel is the smokestack of a ship or engine, the same thing as a chimney.

clue.text: One no longer working on Hebridean island

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped work and gone to live on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word but supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree is a person who has left paid employment for good, usually because of age.

clue.text: Family is concerned about Pinter's last play

parts.note: blood means family or kin, as in 'blood is thicker than water'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worrying word goes around a single letter

parts.note: someone who bothers is troubled or concerned

indicators.note: the last of a name means its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of Pinter

explanation.surface: A family frets over the final work of the playwright Harold Pinter.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinter is a red herring: the play is Willy Russell's musical about twins separated at birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood Brothers is a long-running stage musical by Willy Russell, so it is a play.

clue.text: Together in the past

definitions.meaning: first meaning: simultaneously, all at once
second meaning: formerly, once upon a time

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a couple who used to be together; the phrase actually has two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean simultaneously, as in arriving at one time, or formerly, as in at one time I lived there.

clue.text: Fight scheduled — end of April

parts.note: something due is expected or scheduled

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of April

explanation.surface: A bout has been booked for the last days of April.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, traditionally with swords or pistols.

clue.text: Writer may have question after dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
a point is a matter raised for discussion, a question

explanation.surface: An author has a query to raise after a night out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the question piece second. 'Writer' suggests an author but means a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, a writing instrument, so in crossword terms a writer.

clue.text: Brief man about elected premier

parts.note: to brief someone is to prime them with information

indicators.note: about means around, so the man word surrounds the word for elected

parts.note: mister is the title for a man
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: Someone briefs a man about the person who has just been elected premier.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier is the usual synonym for the head of government, the prime minister.

clue.text: Invigorating air round region

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is an area or region

explanation.surface: Fresh air blowing around a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used informally for the bracing fresh air of the seaside, once thought healthy.

clue.text: Where lots go to join game

parts.note: lots are the items put up for sale at an auction
to bridge is to join two things

explanation.surface: Many people are heading off to take part in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' reads as 'many people', but means items for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is an older form of the card game bridge, in which players bid for the contract.

clue.text: Determined one's position with an editor, upset having received note

indicators.note: having received means taking something in, so a piece goes inside the rearranged letters
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An editor, upset, took his bearings after being sent a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate oneself is to work out where one is in relation to one's surroundings; orientated is the past tense.

clue.text: Garden centre in northern Surrey, flourishing

indicators.note: flourishing suggests being waved about with a flourish, so the county's letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for northern
the county's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A thriving garden centre in the north of the English county of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where plants are grown and sold, essentially a garden centre.

clue.text: Musicians, perhaps, sway Greek publisher

parts.note: to rock is to sway to and fro
GR is an abbreviation for Greek
OUP is Oxford University Press, a publisher

explanation.surface: Musicians who might sway a Greek publishing house.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock group is a band of musicians who play rock; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Nobleman, one meeting the Queen beforehand

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
I is the Roman numeral one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A peer meets the monarch ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier and beforehand both mean at a previous time, so they are adverbial synonyms.

clue.text: Flinches, with reference to snakes

parts.note: re means with reference to
as a verb, a path that snakes winds or coils

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks back when snakes are mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snakes' looks like a noun for the reptiles but works as a verb meaning winds.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring back in fear or disgust, the same reaction as flinching.

clue.text: Appropriate bit

definitions.meaning: first meaning, as a verb: to take for oneself, often sneakily
second meaning: a simple jointed mouthpiece on a horse's bridle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' wants to be an adjective meaning suitable; here it is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is British slang for taking something for oneself, and a snaffle is a type of bridle bit.

clue.text: Sharp end

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests 'the sharp end'; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme describes something severe or acute, and as a noun an extreme is an outermost limit or end.

clue.text: Favour daughter entering English and another language

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the language

parts.note: Norse is the old Scandinavian language
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent backs a daughter's study of English and a second language.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or approve of something, the same as to favour it.

clue.text: How to handle unwanted photo opportunity?

definitions.text: How to handle unwanted photo opportunity?

parts.words: How to handle unwanted photo opportunity?
parts.note: surface reading: advice for when someone points a camera at you unwillingly
setter's reading: the idiom for putting up with something unpleasant, with the smile for the camera as the pun

explanation.walkthrough: The photo context makes you think of smiling for the camera, which is half the phrase; the whole phrase means endure stoically.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accept an unpleasant situation without complaint, and smiling is literally what a photo calls for.

clue.text: Profligate nicking grand, the villain

indicators.note: nicking means stealing and keeping hold of, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a roué is a debauched, dissolute man
G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A wastrel steals a thousand pounds, the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest, unprincipled person, a villain.

clue.text: Transfer to be approved

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to get through a test or vote, as a bill does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a transfer awaiting sign-off; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is both to hand something to another and to be accepted, as an exam or law passes.

clue.text: Engaged in a contest

parts.note: taken as written
a bout is a contest, especially a boxing match

explanation.surface: Taking part in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be about something is to be busy with it, as in go about your business.

clue.text: Caution shown as gift horse put out

indicators.note: put out means upset or disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Wariness about looking a gift horse in the mouth, after the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is thinking ahead about what may go wrong, a form of prudence or caution.

clue.text: Takes over from leading exporter, initially in casual dresses

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the rearranged letters
casual means haphazard or loose, so the letters fall into a new order
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of exporter
the letters taken as written
a team that is leading is up

explanation.surface: A top clothing exporter's informal frocks are replacing the old styles.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces go separately into the rearranged letters of dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to replace or take the place of something older.

clue.text: Study prepared? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: prepared means ready

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a student is prepared, and the answer is nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is the British way of saying to study it at university.
